title: UPI MDR tracker
currentAnswer: UPI MDR is not in effect. A proposed 0.4% charge on merchant payments above Rs 2,000 was scheduled for 15 October 2026, then deferred with no new start date announced. Payments of Rs 2,000 or less remain free, and person-to-person transfers remain free at all values.

whoIsAffected.note: Free at all values. No change has been proposed.
Explicitly excluded from the proposed charge.
A 0.4% MDR was proposed for this band. Deferred, with no announced start date.
A flat Rs 5 per transaction has been reported but not announced publicly by NPCI.

timeline.headline: Flat Rs 5 reported for merchant-to-merchant payments
timeline.detail: Business Standard reported, citing two people aware of the matter, that merchant-to-merchant UPI payments are likely to carry a flat MDR of Rs 5 per transaction. NPCI has not announced this publicly.

timeline.headline: 0.4% proposal detailed, capped at ₹300
timeline.detail: The proposed charge is 0.4% on person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 and above. It is a merchant-side cost and cannot be passed to the customer as a separate fee. Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month by UPI QR remain exempt.

timeline.headline: Still no agreed rollout date
timeline.detail: The government, RBI and NPCI had not reached common ground on timing. Trader resistance and forthcoming state assembly elections were reported as factors, with one report suggesting the rollout could slip past the 2027 state elections.

timeline.headline: Implementation deferred past Diwali
timeline.detail: The UPI and Services Steering Committee postponed the launch, citing the festive season and operational difficulties. No replacement date was given.

timeline.headline: Original scheduled start date
timeline.detail: A 0.4% MDR on selected person-to-merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 was originally scheduled to take effect on this date. It did not come into force.
